gaps.sentence: There are trees on ___ side of the road.
gaps.hint: singular noun: each of the two sides
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means each of the two sides; 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: She made very ___ mistakes in the essay, so she nearly got full marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Very few mistakes' means almost none, which explains the high mark; 'mistakes' is countable.

gaps.sentence: ___ single room in the hotel was fully booked.
gaps.explanation: 'Every single room' is the emphatic collocation meaning 'without exception'.
'Warm enough' means sufficiently warm; 'enough' follows the adjective.
'Luggage' is an uncountable noun, so 'how much' is used.

gaps.sentence: The village is remote and has ___ facilities — not even a post office.
gaps.hint: negative meaning with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Few facilities' means almost none, which matches 'not even a post office'; 'facilities' is countable.

gaps.sentence: I asked ___ in the office, but nobody knew the answer.
gaps.explanation: 'I asked everybody' (all the people) contrasts with 'nobody knew'; 'everything' refers to things, not people.

gaps.sentence: ___ everyone in the office passed the safety test.
gaps.hint: the only adverb that can modify 'everyone'
gaps.explanation: 'Almost everyone' is the standard pattern; 'each', 'all' and 'every' cannot directly precede 'everyone'.
